reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Comic Book Born From Conspiracy Podcasting", "body": "Thomas Gorence and Juan Ayala used the episode to promote The Chosen Juan Versus The Saturnian Cube, an independent comic they were funding on Kickstarter. One guest described it as the first issue of a planned six part series, with each issue tackling a different conspiracy and featuring familiar names from the podcast community. Juan said the work took far more time and money than outsiders assumed, and the guests said they hoped other podcasters would pitch their own comic ideas so creators could cross pollinate in a shared universe. Late in the show, one of the guests reported that the campaign had passed its goal with thirteen days remaining."}, {"title": "Schooling as Conditioning and Pavlovian Bells", "body": "Thomas read a page from one of his comics describing the American school system as government sponsored mind control, pointing to school bells that separate subjects as Pavlovian triggers. Other voices on the panel then offered their own accounts of how compulsory schooling began, tracing it to a Prussian model, and one speaker linked occupational licensing to the same system. Another speaker argued that the word license originally meant an excess of liberty, and called it ironic that it now stood for asking permission. A later speaker said schooling displaced the passing of herb craft and other self reliance skills from parent to child."}, {"title": "Memory Palaces as Magic and Mythology", "body": "The panel traded notes on memory palaces, a technique one participant said Thomas had introduced him to. That participant described a deliberately absurd palace of dill pickles, a silicone door and a scuba diver in a sink, explaining that outrageous images lock memories in place. Participants said ancient bards used the same method to carry epic poems, and one speaker argued that mythology worked this way, with grand sky stories preserved by unforgettable images. Another participant described a friend who walks into tarot cards through a palace of her own, and one participant recalled a childhood nightly visualization that later matched an image of Westminster Abbey."}, {"title": "The Ether, the Akashic Record, and Forgetting", "body": "Chance argued that the aura works like an unconscious mind, recording everything a person has experienced, and that the Akashic record is the ether, an indivisible medium connecting matter, energy and spirit. He claimed this meant the body already holds all knowledge, so that wisdom is remembering rather than learning, and that lessons fade when a person's coherence dips. A panelist compared the Akashic record to a blockchain and noted that an ethernet cable echoes the word ether. Later, another speaker said that coming through the sign of Cancer symbolized a chalice holding a liquid of amnesia, so people were not meant to recall everything at once."}, {"title": "Oz, Labyrinths, and Symbolic Word Play", "body": "A video by Mario Garza read The Wizard of Oz through the four elements and the tarot, matching the Scarecrow to air, the Tin Man to water, Dorothy to earth and the Lion to fire. In it he argued the Tin Man suited the sign of Cancer through his shell, his silvery color and his empty vessel, punning that the word cancer contains can. Chance read a passage from Dylan Saccoccio linking Troy and its fire tower to Cancer, cubes and labyrinths. Thomas said the word labyrinth likely traced to the Minoan double headed axe, and read the Minotaur as the ego to be overcome."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Returning Vibe Ranter Juan Ayala joins us tonight along with Thomas Gorence, AKA Paranoid American, and they have an awesome new project to promote: The Chosen Juan Versus The Saturnian Cube, an independent comic book venture they're launching through Kickstarter. Expect irreverent yet informed conspiratorial commentary as we explore their various areas of research interest.
